summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Greek working source. Both preserve the plant imagery, divided allegiance, lip/heart contrast, repeated life/death negations, idol worship and shame, urgent repentance condition, possibility of life, and already-completed handing over to the women. The simplified edition’s shorter sentences retain these claims. The notes distinguish editorial supplements from reported surviving wording and disclose the consequential alternatives without replacing the selected working reading or harmonizing its difficult assertions. Contextual “repent” follows current policy. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of reported alternatives only; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, independently verify the reported apparatus, or certify exhaustive collation.
